2607.08625.title: The complexities of patient-centred conversational artificial intelligence
2607.08625.paper_summary: Consumer-facing health chatbots powered by large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for symptom assessment. However, chatbot development and evaluation often rely on cooperative, articulate, simulated patients. We analysed 2,053 real patient-chatbot conversations and found that communication patterns and expression of emotions vary widely across users. We developed a patient simulator that separately models clinical content, emotional state, conversational strategy, and communication style. In a Turing-inspired evaluation of realism with 15 human graders, simulated conversations were nearly indistinguishable from real ones, with human graders achieving an accuracy of 55%. We used five distinct patient personae, across 1,164 clinician-graded cases, to evaluate the performance of four LLMs in urgency assessment. We found that communication style can significantly alter triage outcomes. Patient-centred conversational artificial intelligence must accommodate communication diversity: systems designed for idealised, rather than realistic, interactions risk underperforming and amplifying health disparities when deployed in the real world.
2607.08625.paper_summary_zh: 消費者面向的健康聊天機器人由大型語言模型（LLMs）驅動，越來越多地用於症狀評估。<lb/>然而，聊天機器人的開發和評估通常依賴於合作、表達清晰的模擬患者。<lb/>我們分析了2,053個真實患者與聊天機器人的對話，發現用戶之間的溝通模式和情感表達差異很大。<lb/>我們開發了一個患者模擬器，分別建模臨床內容、情感狀態、對話策略和溝通風格。<lb/>在一項受圖靈啟發的現實性評估中，15名人類評分者對模擬對話的辨識度幾乎無法與真實對話區分，人類評分者的準確率達到55%。<lb/>我們使用五種不同的患者角色，在1,164個臨床醫生評分的案例中，評估了四個LLMs在緊急評估中的表現。<lb/>我們發現溝通風格可以顯著改變分診結果。<lb/>以患者為中心的對話人工智慧必須適應溝通的多樣性：為理想化而非現實的互動設計的系統在實際部署時可能表現不佳，並加劇健康差距。
